title: Native/System 内存归因：smaps、showmap、heapprofd、memcg 交叉验证
key_conclusions: Native/System attribution requires cross-validation because no single tool sees every bucket.
heapprofd is strong for malloc stack ownership but weak for mmap, dma-buf, and many system buckets.
smaps/showmap explain mappings while memcg explains charge; neither alone proves producer ownership.
A claimed owner must be validated by post-fix or post-kill movement in buckets, PSI, lmkd, and user experience.
shallow_points: The article does not include real heapprofd traces or Perfetto screenshots.
It does not validate showmap category differences across Android releases.
It does not include real dma-buf/slab/system bucket samples.
It does not provide an automated reconciliation script for smaps, heapprofd, and memcg.
